top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) is a mature, independently reproduced result: the magic-wavelength lattice removes first-order light shift and motional broadening for thousands of atoms, clock-to-clock comparisons across RIKEN, JILA, NIST, PTB, SYRTE and NPL confirm the 1e-18 level, and the systematic shifts are computed from atomic structure theory and then confirmed by experiment. The two-name allocation is clean, provided the citation names the many-atom magic-wavelength lattice and so separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. The topological proposal (P002) is scientifically important but its allocation is unresolved (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, the 3D theorists and Hasan fall outside the trio, and it overlaps the 2016 prize), so I rank it second. A prize is better than none.
